subject: Request: Private/on-prem availability & latency exception for customer-managed WAN
messages:
From: Bridget O'Neill <contracts@altair-med.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: itops@altair-med.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA exception request - Altair Medical

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profiles look promising. We need to raise a contract question before we move to a PO: Altair is deploying Redwood Private into our colo and will manage the WAN edge and QoS shaping between our regional offices and the colo. We have observed periodic tail latency (>1.2s p95 for short bursts) that correlates with our WAN shaping during busy backups.

Because the WAN is customer-controlled, our legal and ops teams want a carve‑out that excludes customer-controlled network tail latency from Redwood's availability/latency obligations for the private deployment. Specifically we are proposing:
- For on-prem / private deployments, exclude latency attributable to Altair-managed WAN/transit from Redwood latency SLOs and from any latency-based credits.
- Reduce the guaranteed availability SLO for the private deployment from 99.95% to 99.5% while the exception is in effect.

I've attached a small diagnostic log showing three incidents last month where latency spiked while backups ran. Is this something Redwood will accept as a contractual exception, or do you need more evidence/wording?

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is prepping the PO once we have agreement on exceptions.

Thanks,
Bridget O'Neill
Sr. Contracts Manager
Altair Medical
[Attachment: network-diagnostic.log]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Bridget O'Neill <contracts@altair-med.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA exception request - Altair Medical

Bridget — thanks for the clear note and for the diagnostic. I copied Soojin (security/compliance) and Marcus (platform) so we can assess operational impact and proposed contract language.

Quick answers up front: we do have a process for customer-managed-infra carve‑outs for Private deployments, but any availability reduction or SLO exclusion needs a documented tech rationale + signoff from Platform and Security. We typically require:
- evidence that the impact is caused by customer-controlled networking (your log is helpful),
- a narrowly scoped exception clause tied to named regions/IP ranges/devices, and
- an operational runbook describing mitigation/fallback (e.g., retries, regional failover).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus / Soojin: can you confirm whether the attached log lines are consistent with external WAN shaping vs. any ingress/load-balancer misconfiguration on Redwood's side?
2) Bridget: if Altair can accept scoped wording and a 90‑day review clause (so we can reassess after telemetry), we can draft an SLA addendum.

Carrier/PO timeline: Bridget, would a draft addendum by end of week meet procurement deadlines?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187
From: itops@altair-med.com <itops@altair-med.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@altair-med.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA exception request - Altair Medical

Marissa — thanks for the rapid reply. We can accept a scoped exception. A few constraints from our side:
- We need the exception to cover a named set of POPs and the three WAN ASN paths used for redundancy.
- We require a quarterly review clause and a mutual telemetry-sharing clause (we will share packet captures/NetFlow for incidents).
- We prefer the 99.5% availability target during the exception window.

We attached a longer diagnostic bundle in the original transmission (separate SFTP link if you need it). Procurement would like the one-page addendum today if possible to move the PO.

Bridget O'Neill
Sr. Contracts Manager
Altair Medical
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA exception request - Altair Medical

Team — I reviewed the log excerpt and Marcus's notes (see inline below). Given Altair's strong compliance posture and their willingness to accept a 90-day review and telemetry-sharing, I approve a scoped exception with the following guardrails:

- Scope: Exception applies only to the specified POPs (us-west-2 colo at 203.0.113.12, us-east-1 colo at 198.51.100.24) and the three ASNs listed in their SOW. Any increase in scope requires an additional review.
- Availability: During the exception window we will commit to 99.5% availability for the Private deployment, with latency-based credits excluded for incidents we determine (via joint runbook analysis) are caused by customer-managed WAN.
- Evidence: Altair must provide packet captures/NetFlow and a three-party incident timeline for any event they claim as excluded.
- Review cadence: 90 days post-execution for telemetry review, then quarterly thereafter until exception is removed.
- Rollback: Redwood retains the right to revoke the exception if telemetry shows misattribution or repeated issues originating inside Redwood-managed infrastructure.

I drafted a one-page addendum (attached) with that language and a DocuSign link for signature. Marcus, Soojin — please validate the technical appendix and runbook link before I send to Bridget. Bridget — if this aligns we will route the addendum for signature and then attach the finalized appendix to the Private deployment SOW.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Product & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sla-exception-addendum-v1.docx]
